title: 2nd sitting of the 20th Majlis
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla; Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim chaired the later voting session
summary: The sitting opened with an urgent motion from the MDP's Ibrahim Nazil on the Addu City water supply failures in Hithadhoo, Maradhoo, Maradhoo-Feydhoo and Feydhoo, which the house voted 83-0 to debate for the one hour allowed. Government-side and opposition members traded views on who is responsible for the water utility's debts and on the new MWSC project and borehole works; the one-hour debate ended with no further decision recorded on the motion. The house then sent three ministerial nominations to the government accountability committee, chose Hussain Riza Adam for the Judicial Service Commission 83-0, and approved non-party members' standing committee seats 88-0. Part of the Hulhudhoo speech was too garbled to follow closely.

items.title: Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: 72 members present, 1 on leave, none on official travel

items.title: Urgent matter under Rule 170: lack of clean piped water in Addu City (Hithadhoo, Maradhoo, Maradhoo-Feydhoo, Feydhoo)
items.outcome: accepted for debate 83-0; debated for one hour, no further decision recorded

items.title: President's nomination of three ministers (Attorney General, Minister of Islamic Affairs, Minister of Housing, Land and Urban Development) sent for the Majlis's consent
items.outcome: referred to the committee on government accountability (Rule 113(b))

items.title: Choosing an MP member of the Judicial Service Commission
items.outcome: Hussain Riza Adam (Maafushi) nominated by Husnee Mubarik, seconded by Abdulla Rifau; passed 83-0

items.title: Election of non-party members to the standing committees (Rule 130(a))
Items for vote
items.outcome: Judicial Service Commission member and standing committee seats both passed; sitting adjourned to 4 June 09:00

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Tabled the urgent motion: about 28,000 Addu residents have had unreliable water since April, facing large bills for little water.
Called on the government and utility to fix the supply, saying the problem is not a result of the past two months.
Raised a point of order saying another member had misread the timeline of the problem.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Questioned the motion's purpose and why the mover did not act during the previous term, citing utility debt figures.
Replied to the point of order that capacity expansion is long-term budgeted work.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Argued the former MDP government and its supermajority bear responsibility for utility debt, and thanked the President for the project.
Seconded the nomination of Hussain Riza Adam to the Judicial Service Commission.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Said the constitution guarantees clean water and questioned the earlier government's contracting of the water works.
Nominated Hussain Riza Adam (Maafushi) for the Judicial Service Commission.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Said the utility's storage went unmaintained under earlier governments and that the current administration has started a 256 million rufiyaa project.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Said the utility was left with about 4 billion rufiyaa of debt and the new project will raise water production and storage capacity ten-fold.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said the government is working in good faith, citing the 286 million rufiyaa project, and blamed past neglect of storage and tanks.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said Addu's water reserve was only three hours and the government changed it to a seven-day reserve through the new project.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Called for earlier utility management to be investigated and penalised, and for services to be restored without delay.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Welcomed the chance to debate the motion and said past governments' dealings and utility debts need to be studied and investigated.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the motion deserves a longer debate than the time allowed and criticised the MDP's record on the utility's finances.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said access to clean water is a constitutional right that cannot be put on hold, and urged a quick solution for Addu residents.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Said basic services such as water and sewerage are constitutional rights and noted similar gaps on islands in his own constituency.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Thanked members for backing the motion and described the water plant problems in Hulhumeedhoo, urging the government to fix them.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said the earlier government did not build adequate water storage and that the utility holds about 4.9 billion rufiyaa of debt.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said Addu City's essential services went unmet during the previous five years and that the current government has started the work.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Urged the government to restore the service now and stop assigning blame, saying residents are bearing the hardship.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Questioned what earlier mega-projects delivered, and cited the President's 282 million rufiyaa project as the way to fix water and sewerage.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abdul Rahman
positions: Welcomed the motion being accepted and said the water problem also affects other islands, with the Majlis ready to help through committees.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Thanked both parliamentary groups for taking up the motion and criticised the MDP's conduct while it held a supermajority.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said the motion was not truly urgent since interim water service was restored on the 12th and a 287 million rufiyaa project is underway.

decisions: House voted 83-0 to debate the urgent Addu City water matter
Three ministerial nominations referred to the government accountability committee
Hussain Riza Adam (Maafushi) chosen as the MP member of the Judicial Service Commission
Non-party members' standing committee seats approved as submitted

votes.what: Debate the urgent matter on Addu City water supply
Hussain Riza Adam as MP member of the Judicial Service Commission
